A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CrossSDF and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and supplementary sections A–B. Retained content can be matched across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on synthetic shapes and real CT scans, including quantitative comparisons, qualitative reconstructions, and component and slice-count ablations.

after.justification: v3 reports original synthetic and real-CT reconstruction results, including retained experiments, additional component ablations, and new volume-IoU measurements.

M1.justification: The adaptive sampler, hybrid hash-grid/Fourier encoder, symmetric-difference loss, and Eikonal and minimum-surface regularization remain unchanged. The additional method variants are ablation controls, not revisions to the proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six thin and six thick synthetic structures, aligned and non-aligned slicing scenarios, and four real CT cases. The additional metric and ablations use retained datasets and tasks.

E2.justification: Existing comparisons retain their baseline membership, including OReX, Screened Poisson, POCO, Neural-IMLS, and the appendix comparison with Bermano et al. The new volume-IoU table evaluates a subset of existing baselines without removing their previously reported comparisons.

E3.justification: v3 adds 3D volume IoU as an evaluation metric for thin synthetic structures in Appendix A.2 and Table A1. Existing slicing configurations, training settings, and CT holdout descriptions remain unchanged; the approximate-10% versus every-sixth-slice inconsistency already appears in v1 Appendix A.1.

E4.justification: v3 Table 4 extends the existing component analysis with removal of minimum-surface regularization, Fourier-only encoding, and L1 loss on Omega_off, across the same four shapes. Earlier component, slice-count, indicator-label, and standard hash-grid analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The additional tables do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v3 adds volume-IoU scores and results for three additional ablations. For example, new Table A1 reports aligned-Alveolis IoU of 0.87 for CrossSDF versus 0.37 for OReX, while non-aligned Heart scores 0.70 versus Screened Poisson's 0.71. Previously reported performance values, including the relocated CT results, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, sample sets, encoding equations, and loss formulations in Equations 1–8 are retained. No new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs accompany the added evaluations.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about thin-structure reconstruction, the three principal method components, the benchmark, and performance on synthetic and real data.

C2.justification: Explanations of laddering, grid artifacts, and baseline failures remain, as do limitations concerning very sparse slices and optimization speed. The additional ablation and IoU entries receive no new substantive interpretation.

D1.justification: v3 adds a project-website link and changes supplementary-video access instructions from an attachment to the website. Appendix B adds 'similarly for competing methods' to the 512^3 marching-cubes extraction statement. These are documentation additions; other implementation details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 46 references and related-work positioning are retained. Changed citation backreferences reflect content relocation, with no added or removed cited work or revised novelty positioning.

P1.justification: There are limited terminology and copy edits, author-footnote adjustments, and reorganization of CT dataset and results paragraphs. The main section structure, appendix organization, and most prose remain intact.

P2.justification: The CT table moves from v1 Table A1 to v3 Table 3; a new volume-IoU table becomes Table A1, and the component-ablation table expands. Figure 6 rearranges existing cropped comparisons into one row and removes the contextual vessel view. Other figures remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The additional ablations test previously unexamined design choices, and volume IoU provides a complementary check of reconstruction quality. Moving the CT results into the main text also improves accessibility. These provide limited but useful gains; the new tests receive little methodological explanation or discussion.
